messages.subject: GOF on a Bayesian model
messages.body_plain:
Hello all,

I want to do a GOF on a Bayesian model, using a function that has already been created by someone else.

I am trying to use the output of a jags model (that is of class jagsUI) to feed the GOF function, but this function requires the input to be a class rjags. Do you know of any way I can transform the jagsUI object into a rjags?

Someone suggested another approach. They suggested to modify the code of the GOF function so it accepts my jagsUI object as an input, but I am not sure how to do this…

Thanks for any help!

Esther

messages.subject: Instructors & Helpers Needed for Carpentries R Geospatial Workshop
messages.subject_clean: Instructors & Helpers Needed for Carpentries R Geospatial Workshop
messages.body_plain:
We’re going to be testing out the new Data Carpentry Geospatial workshop curriculum (http://www.datacarpentry.org/lessons/#geospatial-curriculum) at DIBSI <http://ivory.idyll.org/dibsi/> this year, June 27-28th! I’ve signed up as an instructor and can take the lead on content, so this is a great, low-pressure opportunity to join in as a co-instructor or helper and see how this curriculum works.

While it would be great to have people who are familiar with the Carpentries, additional instructors do not need to be Carpentries’ certified. I can fill you in on the basic guidelines for teaching and helping at these workshops. Co-instructors can choose any amount of curriculum that they’d like to teach, and no one has to teach anything they aren’t comfortable with. There will also be lots of people on hand to help out if/when any problems arise. :)

Helpers are people who work one-on-one with workshop attendees when they have questions or get stuck as they work through the material.

Let me know if you’d like to join in as a co-instructor or helper for this workshop!

Why volunteer to teach or help?  Get teaching experience, give yourself a good reason to finally sit down and learn R for geospatial data, network with other geospatial researchers, give back to the community, get more familiar with the Carpentries, add some skills and service to your CV… I’ll stop here, but you get the idea that there’s a lot of reasons to do this and it will be fun!

Data Carpentry curriculum:  http://www.datacarpentry.org/lessons/#geospatial-curriculum

Data Carpentry Geospatial Data with R:  http://www.datacarpentry.org/r-raster-vector-geospatial/

More info about DIBSI:  http://ivory.idyll.org/dibsi/

Interested?  Questions?  Email me, Michele, at  mmto...@ucdavis.edu

If you’d like to attend this workshop rather than teach, I’ll send along the registration information later today so keep an eye on your email.

Michele

Meet and Analyze Data (MAD) is a forum to bring your biological big
data and discuss high level concept problems (what is metagenome
assembly?) and low level coding problems (what does this error message
even mean?!) and everything in between. There is no scheduled or
specific activity: people show up with questions about how to analyze
their data, or maybe they are willing to help others. We typically get
questions about experimental design for
transcriptomic/metagenomic/genomic projects, or how to install
software, or how to run their analysis on clusters or the cloud.

--
Luiz Irber

Ph.D Student
Department of Computer Science
Lab for Data Intensive Biology
University of California, Davis

messages.subject: Five computational workshops, June 27-28, 2018.
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

we are proud to be offering 5 Software and Data Carpentry Workshops at DIBSI this year!

These entry-level 2-day workshops will take place on June 27-28 (Weds-Thurs) in Valley Hall on the UC Davis Veterinary School campus. No previous experience with programming is required to attend.

We are particularly excited to be offering three workshops in areas with newly developed curriculum: Data Carpentry Geospatial and Social Sciences as well as a new Spanish language version of a Software Carpentry workshop, teaching Unix, Git, and R! In addition, we will be offering the same Software Carpentry workshop in English as well as a Data Carpentry Genomics lesson.

Registration is now open! There is a $10 fee which can be paid using a credit card or UC Davis grant number. A fee waiver may be requested by contacting dibsi.t...@gmail.com.

Registration and workshop web sites are here:

Geospatial: https://dib-lab.github.io/2018-06-27-DIBSI-Geospatial/ , https://registration.genomecenter.ucdavis.edu/events/DIBSI_2018_Geospatial_Workshop/

Social Sciences: https://dib-lab.github.io/2018-06-27-DIBSI-SocialSci/ , https://registration.genomecenter.ucdavis.edu/events/DIBSI_2018_SocSci_Workshop/

Spanish Software Carpentry (Unix/Git/R): https://dib-lab.github.io/2018-06-27-SpanishSWC/ , https://registration.genomecenter.ucdavis.edu/events/DIBSI_2018_SWC_Spanish_Workshop/

English Software Carpentry (Unix/Git/R): https://dib-lab.github.io/2018-06-27-DIBSI-SWC/ , https://registration.genomecenter.ucdavis.edu/events/DIBSI_2018_SWC_Workshop/

Genomics: https://dib-lab.github.io/2018-06-27-DIBSI-Genomics/ .https://registration.genomecenter.ucdavis.edu/events/DIBSI_2018_Genomics_Workshop/

Contact dibsi-t...@gmail.com with questions! We hope to see you there!

-----

Estamos muy orgullosos de introducir el taller de Software Carpentry en español!

Tenemos el objetivo de ayudar a los investigadores a realizar su trabajo en menos tiempo y con menos dolor, al enseñarles habilidades básicas de informática y de investigación. Este taller práctico cubrirá los conceptos y herramientas básicos, incluyendo: diseño de programas, el control de versiones, la gestión de datos y la automatización de tareas. Aprenderás a usar la terminal de Unix, Git y R.

No es necesario que tengas ningún conocimiento previo de las herramientas que se presentarán en el taller.

Se alentará a los participantes a ayudarse mutuamente y aplicar lo que han aprendido a sus propios problemas de investigación.

Más información sobre este taller: https://dib-lab.github.io/2018-06-27-SpanishSWC/
Registrarse aquí: https://registration.genomecenter.ucdavis.edu/events/DIBSI_2018_SWC_Spanish_Workshop/

Por favor contactar a dibsi.t...@gmail.com con preguntas

We’re excited to be offering a workshop using the newly released Data Carpentry Social Sciences curriculum! This will be run concurrently with several other Carpentries workshops in association with our Data Intensive Biology Summer Institute (DIBSI). We are currently looking for co-instructors and helpers for this workshop. And, if you’d like to refer anyone to attend the workshop as a learner, registration is now open! See below for details.

Join us as a co-instructor! This is a low-pressure opportunity to try your hand at teaching a small portion of this new curriculum. Carpentries certification is not necessary – we can get you up to speed on the basics of our teaching practices.

Join us as a helper! This is a great experience for anyone with a little skill (or a lot!). Helpers often learn new tips and tricks, as well as gaining confidence, exposure, and appreciation! The more the merrier in this category – helpers play a key role in Carpentries workshops.

About the workshop:
The Data Carpentry Social Sciences workshop teaches data management and analysis for social science research. Learners gain experience with common file formats, tools, and programming languages used in survey-based social science research. You will learn how to perform critical steps in the data analysis lifecycle reproducibly, saving yourself the tedium of performing repetitive and error-prone tasks by hand. From formatting your data in ways that make it easy to work with, to data cleaning and visualization, you will get hands-on practice applying these tools to real-world survey data to solve common analysis problems.

After the workshop, participants will be able to:

	• Use a spreadsheet program to format data tables in a computer-readable way.

	• Use OpenRefine to reproducibly clean messy data.

	• Use the R dplyr package to filter and subset datasets.

	• Use the R ggplot package to visualize data.

This workshop uses a teaching version of a real data set from the SAFI (Studying African Farmer-Led Irrigation) project - a survey study of farming and irrigation methods in Tanzania and Mozambique.

Want more information?

The workshop website is here: https://dib-lab.github.io/2018-06-27-DIBSI-SocialSci/

Registration is available here: https://registration.genomecenter.ucdavis.edu/events/DIBSI_2018_SocSci_Workshop/

Please contact Karen Word at krli...@ucdavis.edu
